words.enDefinition: a plan for managing your own income and expenses

examples.en: I made a personal budget before signing up for any paid societies.
examples.zh: 我先做了份「个人预算」，才决定报名哪些收费社团。

examples.en: My personal budget shows how much I can put toward a trip home.
examples.zh: 我的「个人预算」上列出了我能拿多少钱用来回家一趟。

words.enDefinition: a plan for income and spending over one month

examples.en: My monthly budget is tighter in June because I work fewer hours during exams.
examples.zh: 六月考试期间我打工时间少了，所以这个月的「月度预算」更紧。

examples.en: I left haircuts out of my monthly budget and had to revise it.
examples.zh: 我做「月度预算」的时候忘了把理发的钱算进去，只好改了一下。

words.enDefinition: a spending plan covering one academic semester

examples.en: I put field trips in my semester budget as soon as the dates were announced.
examples.zh: 实地考察的日期一公布，我就把这笔开销加进了「学期预算」。

examples.en: Our student money adviser helped me build a semester budget around three grant payments.
examples.zh: 学校的理财顾问帮我根据分三次发放的助学金做了一份「学期预算」。

words.enDefinition: the amount set aside for food and everyday groceries

examples.en: My grocery budget stretches further when I plan meals around what I already have.
examples.zh: 我用家里现有的食材安排三餐，「食品杂货预算」就更经花。

examples.en: We raised our grocery budget after discovering how often we cooked for friends.
examples.zh: 发现我们经常做饭招待朋友后，我们提高了「食品杂货预算」。

words.enDefinition: the maximum amount someone is allowed or plans to spend

examples.en: We set a spending limit of twenty pounds each for the end-of-term gift exchange.
examples.zh: 我们给期末交换礼物定了「支出上限」，每人二十英镑。

examples.en: My spending limit for a used desk is lower now that I need a lamp too.
examples.zh: 现在我还得买台灯，所以买二手书桌的「支出上限」更低了。

words.enDefinition: a group of expenses of the same type

examples.en: I added a spending category for sports because gym visits were starting to add up.
examples.zh: 去健身房的开销开始多起来，我就新建了一个运动「开支类别」。

examples.en: Food is my biggest spending category after rent, especially when I have evening classes.
examples.zh: 房租之外，伙食是我花钱最多的「开支类别」，特别是有晚课的时候。

words.enDefinition: a list showing how planned spending is divided

examples.en: The budget breakdown shows what we can spend on food, train tickets, and accommodation.
examples.zh: 「预算明细」列出了我们能在餐饮、火车票和住宿上各花多少钱。

examples.en: I shared the budget breakdown so my friends could see why we changed hotels.
examples.zh: 我把「预算明细」发给朋友，让他们明白我们为什么换了酒店。

words.enDefinition: a document for listing income and planning expenses

examples.en: The campus advice office sent me a budget worksheet with separate spaces for weekly expenses.
examples.zh: 学校咨询处发给我一张「预算工作表」，上面有专门填写每周开销的栏目。

examples.en: I left the income box blank on my budget worksheet until I got my work schedule.
examples.zh: 我直到拿到排班表才填「预算工作表」里的收入栏。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of how much will be spent in the future

examples.en: I revised my spending forecast after our course added an extra trip in May.
examples.zh: 课程增加了一次五月的出行后，我就调整了「支出预测」。

examples.en: The spending forecast accounts for higher grocery prices during my placement in the city.
examples.zh: 「支出预测」把我在城里实习期间较高的食品杂货价格也考虑了进去。

words.enDefinition: a check of how well a spending plan is working

examples.en: A budget review showed that I was spending more at the café than on groceries.
examples.zh: 做了一次「预算复盘」，我才发现自己在咖啡馆花的钱比采购食品杂货还多。

examples.en: I'll do a budget review once I know how much the new commute actually costs.
examples.zh: 等我弄清新的通勤路线实际要花多少，就做一次「预算复盘」。

words.enDefinition: extra room in a budget for unexpected costs

examples.en: I left a budget buffer in case the train tickets cost more than expected.
examples.zh: 我留了一点「预算余量」，以防火车票比预想的贵。

examples.en: The budget buffer covered a replacement charger without changing my plans for groceries.
examples.zh: 我用「预算余量」买了个新充电器，没影响买菜的安排。

words.enDefinition: dividing money into separate envelopes for different types of spending

examples.en: I tried envelope budgeting with labelled envelopes for groceries, transport, and evenings out.
examples.zh: 我试了试「信封预算法」，把买菜、交通和晚间聚会的钱分别装进贴好标签的信封。

examples.en: Digital envelope budgeting helped me see what was left for food after my weekly shop.
examples.zh: 用电子版「信封预算法」，我能看到每周采购后还能在吃的方面花多少钱。

words.enDefinition: a budget that assigns a purpose to every unit of income

examples.en: My zero-based budget gives every dollar a job, including the money for next month's trip.
examples.zh: 我的「零基预算」给每一块钱都安排了用途，包括下个月旅行的钱。

examples.en: We used a zero-based budget to decide where this month's part-time wages should go.
examples.zh: 我们用「零基预算」安排了这个月兼职工资的各项用途。

words.enDefinition: carry unspent money forward into the next period

examples.en: This app lets me roll over unused funds from groceries into next month's food budget.
examples.zh: 这个应用可以把我买食品杂货的「未用资金结转」到下个月的伙食预算。

examples.en: We can roll over unused funds from this week's trip to the next one.
examples.zh: 我们可以把本周出行的「未用资金结转」到下一次出行。

collocations: roll over unused funds to next month
roll over unused funds from last term
let you roll over unused funds

words.enDefinition: reduce your spending because money is limited

examples.en: You may have to tighten your belt while the café cuts back your shifts.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆减少你班次的这段时间，你可能得「勒紧裤腰带」过日子。

examples.en: It's hard to tighten your belt when every friend wants to meet over dinner.
examples.zh: 朋友们都想约饭的时候，想「勒紧裤腰带」可真难。

collocations: tighten your belt for a few months

words.enDefinition: with very little money available to spend

examples.en: We managed to spend a weekend in Edinburgh on a shoestring by taking the overnight bus.
examples.zh: 我们坐夜班大巴去爱丁堡过了个周末，「没花多少钱」。

examples.en: Maya ran the student film night on a shoestring by borrowing a projector.
examples.zh: 玛雅借到了一台投影仪，「花很少的钱」就办成了学生电影之夜。

words.enDefinition: keep your spending within what you can afford

examples.en: It takes planning to live within your means when your hours change every week.
examples.zh: 每周工时都在变，想「量入为出」就得提前盘算。

examples.en: Living near campus makes it easier to live within your means if you rarely need transport.
examples.zh: 如果基本不用坐车，住在学校附近就比较容易做到「量入为出」。

collocations: learn to live within your means
try to live within your means
manage to live within your means

words.enDefinition: have just enough money to cover your needs

examples.en: I'm picking up one extra shift this month to make ends meet until payday.
examples.zh: 这月我多上一个班，好「勉强维持生计」撑到发薪日。

examples.en: It got harder to make ends meet after the cheapest supermarket near campus closed.
examples.zh: 学校附近最便宜的超市关门后，想「勉强维持生计」就更难了。

words.enDefinition: manage to live with a limited amount of money

examples.en: I could get by on one shift a week when I lived with family.
examples.zh: 跟家人住的时候，「靠每周上一个班挣的钱就能过日子」。

examples.en: How do students get by on so little when groceries cost this much here?
examples.zh: 这里买菜这么贵，学生怎么「靠这么点钱过日子」？

collocations: get by on a small income

words.enDefinition: make the money available in a budget go further

examples.en: You can stretch your budget by sharing the cost of a tool with your flatmates.
examples.zh: 跟室友分摊工具的钱，就能「让预算更经用」。

examples.en: If you want to stretch your budget this weekend, the city museum is free.
examples.zh: 周末想「让预算更经用」的话，可以去免费的市博物馆。

collocations: find ways to stretch your budget
stretch your budget a little further

words.enDefinition: follow a spending plan without going over it

examples.en: I find it easier to stick to a budget when I bring snacks to campus.
examples.zh: 我自己带零食去学校时，更容易「按预算花钱」。

examples.en: It's tough to stick to a budget when most of your classmates eat out.
examples.zh: 同学大多出去吃饭的话，就很难坚持「按预算花钱」。

collocations: try to stick to a budget
learn to stick to a budget
find it hard to stick to a budget

words.enDefinition: spend much more than the amount that was planned

examples.en: We didn't want to blow the budget on one dinner during the reading break.
examples.zh: 我们不想在阅读周吃一顿饭就「把预算花超一大截」。

examples.en: One last-minute train ticket could blow the budget for the entire weekend away.
examples.zh: 一张临时买的火车票就可能让整个周末的出行「严重超支」。

collocations: try not to blow the budget

words.enDefinition: inexpensive enough for someone with limited money

examples.en: The café has a budget-friendly lunch if you get there before two.
examples.zh: 两点前到的话，这家咖啡馆有「实惠的」午餐。

examples.en: Our adviser listed budget-friendly places to stay within walking distance of the conference venue.
examples.zh: 导师列出了一些「实惠的」住处，走路就能到会议地点。

words.enDefinition: spending that goes beyond the amount originally planned

examples.en: The higher train fares caused a budget overrun on our shared weekend trip.
examples.zh: 火车票涨价导致我们这次结伴周末出游「预算超支」。

examples.en: We each paid a little more to cover the budget overrun for the shared dinner.
examples.zh: 为了补上聚餐「预算超支」的部分，我们每个人都多付了一点。

words.enDefinition: money a spending plan can still accommodate

examples.en: Do we have room in the budget for a taxi if it rains tonight?
examples.zh: 如果今晚下雨，我们还有没有打车的「预算空间」？

examples.en: I checked whether there was room in the budget for one more driving lesson.
examples.zh: 我查了一下，看看还有没有再上一节驾校课的「预算空间」。

collocations: find room in the budget for something

words.enDefinition: a small amount of flexibility in a plan

examples.en: I kept a little wiggle room in case the bus fare went up again.
examples.zh: 我留了点「腾挪余地」，以防公交车票再涨价。

examples.en: Skipping the takeaway gave me a little wiggle room to buy a birthday card.
examples.zh: 少吃一顿外卖，就能留出一点「腾挪余地」买张生日卡。

words.enDefinition: have no money left to spend

examples.en: I don't want to run out of money halfway through my trip home.
examples.zh: 我不想回家的路才走一半就「把钱花光」。

examples.en: When did you realise you might run out of money before the next pay date?
examples.zh: 你什么时候意识到可能还没到下次发薪日就会「把钱花光」？

collocations: run out of money before payday
be about to run out of money

words.enDefinition: there is very little money available to spend

examples.en: Money is tight this week because I had to replace my bike lock.
examples.zh: 我这周不得不换了把自行车锁，所以「手头比较拮据」。

examples.en: If money is tight, we can meet at my place instead of the café.
examples.zh: 要是「手头拮据」，我们可以在我家碰面，不用去咖啡馆。

words.enDefinition: regular expenses whose amounts stay roughly the same

examples.en: I listed my fixed expenses first because my phone plan costs the same every month.
examples.zh: 我先列了「固定支出」，因为手机套餐每月都是同一个价。

examples.en: Once I cover my fixed expenses, I know what is left for nights out.
examples.zh: 付完「固定支出」，我就知道晚上出去玩还能花多少钱。

words.enDefinition: expenses whose amounts change from one period to another

examples.en: My variable expenses rise during exams because I buy coffee on campus more often.
examples.zh: 考试期间我更常在学校买咖啡，所以「浮动支出」会上升。

examples.en: I underestimated my variable expenses because May included several trips to visit friends.
examples.zh: 我低估了「浮动支出」，没想到五月要跑好几趟去看朋友。

words.enDefinition: expenses that come up repeatedly at regular intervals

examples.en: I put all my recurring expenses in one list so I wouldn't miss annual renewals.
examples.zh: 我把所有「经常性支出」列在一起，免得漏掉每年续订的项目。

examples.en: Even small recurring expenses can take up a large part of a student's budget.
examples.zh: 金额不大的「经常性支出」加起来也可能占学生预算的很大一部分。

words.enDefinition: spending on things you need for daily life

examples.en: My bursary covers essential spending such as groceries and bus trips to campus.
examples.zh: 我的助学金够付买菜、坐公交去学校等「必要支出」。

examples.en: We worked out how much essential spending we had before planning the weekend away.
examples.zh: 我们计划周末出游前，先算了算有多少「必要支出」。

words.enDefinition: spending on things you can choose to go without

examples.en: I reduced my discretionary spending by going to fewer concerts this term.
examples.zh: 我这学期少听了几场音乐会，以减少「可选消费支出」。

examples.en: The chart puts streaming and cinema tickets under discretionary spending for this month.
examples.zh: 这张图把流媒体订阅和电影票列在本月的「可选消费支出」里。

words.enDefinition: a single purchase with no recurring payments

examples.en: The software is available as a one-time purchase if you only need the basic version.
examples.zh: 只需要基础版的话，这款软件可以「一次性购买」。

examples.en: I made a one-time purchase because I needed the app for just one assignment.
examples.zh: 我只需要用那个应用完成一次作业，所以选了「一次性购买」。

words.enDefinition: a cost that was not included in your plans

examples.en: The bike repair was an unplanned expense the week before my trip home.
examples.zh: 回家前一周，修自行车成了一笔「计划外支出」。

examples.en: An unplanned expense threw off my budget after I cracked my laptop screen.
examples.zh: 电脑屏幕裂了，换屏这笔「计划外支出」打乱了我的预算。

words.enDefinition: the money you spend on basic daily needs

examples.en: My part-time job covers most of my living expenses during the summer break.
examples.zh: 暑假期间，我的兼职收入能支付大部分「生活开支」。

examples.en: We compared our living expenses after moving from residence to a shared flat.
examples.zh: 从学生宿舍搬到合租公寓后，我们比了一下彼此的「生活开支」。

words.enDefinition: the general cost of meeting everyday needs in a place

examples.en: I noticed the cost of living was higher near my placement than near campus.
examples.zh: 我发现实习地点附近的「生活成本」比学校附近高。

examples.en: The cost of living matters as much as the tuition when I compare universities.
examples.zh: 我比较学校时，「生活成本」和学费一样重要。

words.enDefinition: the total amount of money you spend each month

examples.en: I added up my monthly outgoings to see whether I could afford another language class.
examples.zh: 我算了一下「每月总支出」，看看还能不能再报一门语言课。

examples.en: My monthly outgoings increased when I started commuting to my placement twice a week.
examples.zh: 我开始每周去实习地点两次以后，「每月总支出」就涨了。

words.enDefinition: a small amount regularly given for personal spending

examples.en: My parents still send me a little pocket money while I study abroad.
examples.zh: 我在国外上学，爸妈还是会给我一点「零花钱」。

examples.en: I saved up my pocket money to buy a used camera before the trip.
examples.zh: 我攒了「零花钱」，打算旅行前买台二手相机。

collocations: a weekly amount of pocket money

words.enDefinition: money available for small personal purchases or activities

examples.en: The field trip includes lunch, but I brought some spending money for postcards.
examples.zh: 实地考察包午饭，但我还是带了些「可以自己花的钱」买明信片。

examples.en: I've got enough spending money left for coffee and a museum ticket this afternoon.
examples.zh: 我剩下的「可随意花的钱」够今天下午买咖啡和一张博物馆门票。

words.enDefinition: money provided specifically to cover the cost of food

examples.en: The course gives us a small food allowance on days we work off campus.
examples.zh: 课程安排我们到校外工作时，会给我们一点「伙食补助」。

examples.en: I asked whether the food allowance would cover dinner on the last fieldwork day.
examples.zh: 我问「伙食补助」包不包括实地考察最后一天的晚饭。

words.enDefinition: income left after taxes and mandatory contributions are paid

examples.en: My disposable income went up after I started taking weekend shifts at the café.
examples.zh: 开始在咖啡馆上周末班后，我的「可支配收入」增加了。

examples.en: The survey asks about disposable income before it asks how much students spend on rent.
examples.zh: 这份问卷先问学生的「可支配收入」，再问他们在房租上花多少钱。

words.enDefinition: income that varies in amount or arrives inconsistently

examples.en: It's hard to plan around irregular income when the café posts shifts every Sunday.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆每周日才公布班次，想按「不稳定收入」做计划挺难。

examples.en: I have irregular income from tutoring because some weeks nobody books a lesson.
examples.zh: 我做家教的「收入不稳定」，因为有些星期根本没人预约。

words.enDefinition: money or help with costs provided by family members

examples.en: I listed family support separately because my parents only help with groceries and books.
examples.zh: 我把「家人经济支持」单独列出来，因为爸妈只帮我付买菜和买书的钱。

examples.en: It's harder to take an unpaid placement without family support for rent and food.
examples.zh: 如果「家里不帮忙负担」房租和伙食费，就更难去做无薪实习。

words.enDefinition: the regular ways in which someone spends money

examples.en: My spending habits changed when I stopped passing the bakery on my way home.
examples.zh: 回家路上不再经过那家面包店后，我的「消费习惯」变了。

examples.en: We talked about spending habits at a campus workshop for students in their first year.
examples.zh: 我们在学校给大一学生办的讲座上聊了「消费习惯」。

words.enDefinition: a recurring trend in when or where money is spent

examples.en: Looking at my receipts, I spotted a spending pattern: I shopped most often after late classes.
examples.zh: 看了小票，我发现一个「支出规律」：上完晚课后我最常买东西。

examples.en: My spending pattern changes during exams when I commute less and order more food.
examples.zh: 考试期间，我通勤少了、外卖点多了，「支出规律」也跟着变了。

words.enDefinition: a tool that shows how much you have spent

examples.en: My spending tracker shows I spend more on the days I forget my lunch.
examples.zh: 我的「支出记录工具」显示，忘带午饭的那几天我花得更多。

examples.en: I made a spending tracker in a spreadsheet when the app stopped syncing properly.
examples.zh: 应用同步出了问题，我就用电子表格做了个「支出记录工具」。

words.enDefinition: regularly check what you spend and how much

examples.en: It's easier to keep track of your spending when most receipts are in one place.
examples.zh: 把大多数收据放在一起，更容易「留意自己的开支」。

examples.en: Do you keep track of your spending on the weeks you pay mostly in cash?
examples.zh: 你大部分时候用现金的那几周，也会「留意自己的开支」吗？

collocations: find a way to keep track of your spending
help you keep track of your spending
easily keep track of your spending

words.enDefinition: enter the details of a payment in a record

examples.en: I forgot to log an expense when I paid cash at the train station.
examples.zh: 我在火车站用现金付款时，忘了「记下那笔开支」。

examples.en: You can log an expense before the receipt fades or gets lost in your bag.
examples.zh: 你可以趁收据还没褪色、也没在包里弄丢时，「把那笔开支记下来」。

collocations: log an expense in an app

words.enDefinition: assign something you bought to a spending group

examples.en: I don't know how to categorize a purchase that includes both food and stationery.
examples.zh: 一张小票上既有食品又有文具，我不知道怎么「给这笔消费分类」。

examples.en: The app can categorize a purchase automatically, but it sometimes gets campus cafés wrong.
examples.zh: 应用可以自动「给一笔消费分类」，只是有时会把校园咖啡馆的消费分错。

words.enDefinition: a physical or digital folder for storing receipts

examples.en: I keep a receipt folder on my phone for things I might need to return.
examples.zh: 我在手机上建了个「收据文件夹」，存放可能要退货的购物收据。

examples.en: Our house has a receipt folder by the door for anything we buy together.
examples.zh: 我们在住处门边放了一个「收据文件夹」，大家一起买东西的收据都放进去。

collocations: keep it in your receipt folder

words.enDefinition: a record of things you have bought before

examples.en: I checked my purchase history to see when I last bought a printer cartridge.
examples.zh: 我查了「购买记录」，看上次是什么时候买的打印机墨盒。

examples.en: The shop's purchase history showed two orders for the same refill pack last month.
examples.zh: 店里的「购买记录」显示，上个月同样的补充装下了两单。

words.enDefinition: the amount really spent rather than the amount planned

examples.en: Our actual spending on food exceeded the estimate during the second week of fieldwork.
examples.zh: 实地考察第二周，我们在伙食上的「实际支出」超过了预估。

examples.en: I put actual spending in a different column so I could quickly spot the gap.
examples.zh: 我把「实际支出」放在另一栏，这样一眼就能看出差额。

collocations: compare actual spending with the budget

words.enDefinition: the amount spent since the start of the current year

examples.en: My year-to-date spending includes the conference ticket I paid for back in January.
examples.zh: 我的「本年累计支出」包括一月份就付过的会议门票。

examples.en: I checked my year-to-date spending before deciding whether to renew the sports club membership.
examples.zh: 决定要不要续体育社团会籍前，我查了「本年累计支出」。

words.enDefinition: the sum of amounts at the end of the month

examples.en: I waited for the last grocery receipt before calculating our month-end total for food.
examples.zh: 我等最后一张买菜小票到了，才算我们伙食费的「月底合计金额」。

examples.en: The month-end total included two bus passes because I bought one early for June.
examples.zh: 「月底合计金额」里有两张公交月票，因为我提前买了六月份那张。

words.enDefinition: a list showing how actual spending is divided among categories

examples.en: My spending breakdown showed that most of my food money went to takeaway lunches.
examples.zh: 「支出明细」显示，我的伙食费大多花在了外卖午饭上。

examples.en: I added a spending breakdown to the spreadsheet so I could compare different months.
examples.zh: 我在表格里加了「支出明细」，方便比较不同月份。

words.enDefinition: money spent using notes and coins

examples.en: My cash spending looked low because I had forgotten to record purchases at the market.
examples.zh: 我忘了记下在市场买东西的钱，所以「现金支出」看起来很少。

examples.en: I record cash spending at the end of each day while I still remember it.
examples.zh: 我每天结束前趁还记得，把当天的「现金支出」记下来。

words.enDefinition: costs paid together by people who live in the same home

examples.en: We use a spreadsheet for shared household expenses like washing-up liquid and bin bags.
examples.zh: 我们用电子表格记洗洁精、垃圾袋之类的「合住共同开销」。

examples.en: My flatmates and I keep shared household expenses separate from our own grocery bills.
examples.zh: 我和室友把「合住共同开销」和各自买菜的钱分开算。

words.enDefinition: the amount each person pays for a shared purchase or activity

examples.en: The per-person cost fell once two classmates joined our booking for the weekend trip.
examples.zh: 又有两个同学加入我们周末的出行预订后，「人均费用」降了。

examples.en: I worked out the per-person cost before asking everyone to pay for the shared dinner.
examples.zh: 我先算好「人均费用」，才请大家把聚餐的钱付了。

words.enDefinition: a day when you deliberately avoid spending money

examples.en: I packed a sandwich before class so I could stick to my no-spend day.
examples.zh: 上课前我带了个三明治，好完成那天的「零消费日」。

examples.en: We had a no-spend day and played football instead of going to the cinema.
examples.zh: 我们过了个「零消费日」，没有去看电影，改去踢球了。

words.enDefinition: a temporary stop on some or all spending

examples.en: I put a spending freeze on clothes until I'd paid for my ticket home.
examples.zh: 在买好回家的票之前，我「暂停了衣物支出」。

examples.en: Our society lifted its spending freeze when the next round of funding came through.
examples.zh: 新一轮经费到账后，我们社团结束了「暂停支出」的安排。

words.enDefinition: something bought suddenly without planning or thinking it through

examples.en: The mug was an impulse buy that I regretted by the time I got home.
examples.zh: 这个马克杯是我「一时冲动买的」，还没到家就后悔了。

examples.en: I kept the receipt because the jacket was an impulse buy after my last exam.
examples.zh: 那件夹克是考完最后一门「一时冲动买的」，所以我留了小票。

words.enDefinition: spend unusually freely on something you want

examples.en: I decided to splurge on a nice dinner after surviving my first exam week.
examples.zh: 熬过第一次考试周后，我决定「大手笔花钱」吃顿好的。

examples.en: We don't usually splurge on hotels, but this one was right next to the station.
examples.zh: 我们平时不在酒店上「花大钱」，不过这家就在车站旁边。

words.enDefinition: buy or do something enjoyable as a reward for yourself

examples.en: You could treat yourself to brunch after you hand in the last assignment.
examples.zh: 交完最后一份作业，你可以吃顿早午餐「犒劳一下自己」。

examples.en: It's nice to treat yourself to a coffee after a long morning in the lab.
examples.zh: 在实验室忙了一上午，买杯咖啡「犒劳一下自己」挺不错。

collocations: treat yourself to a good meal

words.enDefinition: shopping done to make yourself feel better

examples.en: I joked that my new notebook was retail therapy after a difficult week.
examples.zh: 我开玩笑说，这本新笔记本是我那周过得不顺时「买来解闷」的。

examples.en: She went for a walk instead of going into town for some retail therapy.
examples.zh: 她出去散了个步，没有进城「购物解闷」。

collocations: go out for some retail therapy

words.enDefinition: many inexpensive purchases can total a large amount

examples.en: Small purchases add up when I grab a snack after every evening lecture.
examples.zh: 每次上完晚课我都买点零食，「小额消费就这样积少成多」。

examples.en: My receipts showed that small purchases add up much faster than I thought.
examples.zh: 小票让我发现，「小额消费积少成多」的速度比我想得快得多。

collocations: see how small purchases add up
realize that small purchases add up
small purchases add up over time

words.enDefinition: check what different sellers charge for the same thing

examples.en: I wanted to compare prices before buying the same winter coat my flatmate had.
examples.zh: 我想先「比较价格」，再买一件和室友一样的冬外套。

examples.en: We always compare prices across two supermarkets before doing a big shop together.
examples.zh: 我们一起大量采购之前，总会先「比一比两家超市的价格」。

words.enDefinition: purchase a large quantity at the same time

examples.en: We buy in bulk when rice is cheaper and split the bags between three flats.
examples.zh: 大米便宜的时候我们会「大量采购」，然后分给三个住处。

examples.en: It made sense to buy in bulk once I had somewhere to store everything.
examples.zh: 有地方存货之后，「大量采购」就划算了。

collocations: buy in bulk to save money

words.enDefinition: buy things during periods when shops reduce prices

examples.en: I usually shop the sales for winter clothes because campus gets cold by October.
examples.zh: 我通常「趁打折买」冬装，因为学校到了十月就开始冷。

examples.en: We usually shop the sales for the basics we need when we move.
examples.zh: 搬家需要的日用品，我们通常「趁打折时买」。

words.enDefinition: goods sold under a widely recognized brand name

examples.en: I stopped buying brand-name products once I found a cheaper cereal I actually liked.
examples.zh: 找到一种更便宜又合口味的谷物早餐后，我就不买「知名品牌商品」了。

examples.en: The student shop carries a few brand-name products alongside cheaper versions of the same items.
examples.zh: 学生商店在卖一些「知名品牌商品」的同时，也卖同类的便宜款。

words.enDefinition: goods sold under the retailer's own brand name

examples.en: I buy own-brand products when the ingredients look similar and the price is lower.
examples.zh: 配料差不多、价格又更低时，我会买「自有品牌商品」。

examples.en: This supermarket sells own-brand products in plain boxes near the bottom of the shelf.
examples.zh: 这家超市把包装简朴的「自有品牌商品」放在货架靠下的位置。

words.enDefinition: look for and buy things that someone has already owned

examples.en: I started to shop secondhand after seeing how much new winter clothes cost here.
examples.zh: 看到这里的新冬装那么贵，我就开始「买二手」了。

examples.en: If you shop secondhand, you can sometimes find a desk near campus for very little.
examples.zh: 如果愿意「买二手」，有时可以在学校附近花很少的钱买到书桌。

words.enDefinition: only the things that are absolutely needed

examples.en: I bought only the bare essentials because my first weekend shift got cancelled.
examples.zh: 第一个周末的班被取消了，所以我只买了「最基本的必需品」。

examples.en: We picked up the bare essentials before unpacking the boxes in our new flat.
examples.zh: 拆新公寓里的箱子前，我们先买了「最基本的必需品」。

words.enDefinition: try to find something offered at a good price

examples.en: I'll look for a deal on train tickets when I know which weekend works.
examples.zh: 确定好哪个周末有空后，我会「找找划算的」火车票。

examples.en: We decided to look for a deal before paying to replace our microwave.
examples.zh: 花钱换微波炉之前，我们决定先「找找划算的优惠」。

collocations: look for a deal on tickets
help someone look for a deal

words.enDefinition: a seller's agreement to charge the same lower price as a competitor
acceptedZhAnswers: 商家按竞争对手的低价销售

examples.en: I asked for a price match after finding the same calculator for less elsewhere.
examples.zh: 我查到别处同款计算器更便宜，就问这家能不能「按对方的低价卖」。

examples.en: The campus shop offered a price match, so I bought the printer there after class.
examples.zh: 学校商店愿意「按对手的低价卖」，我就下课后在那里买了打印机。

words.enDefinition: worth the price because of the quality or quantity

examples.en: The fixed lunch menu is good value for money if you're already near the library.
examples.zh: 如果你就在图书馆附近，这个午餐套餐挺「物有所值」的。

examples.en: A used bike was good value for money compared with paying for buses all year.
examples.zh: 和一整年坐公交的花销比起来，买辆二手自行车「物有所值」。

words.enDefinition: benefit enough from something to justify what you paid

examples.en: You get your money's worth from the pass if you take the bus every day.
examples.zh: 如果你每天都坐公交，这张通票就「买得值」。

examples.en: It's hard to get your money's worth from that gym during the exam period.
examples.zh: 考试期间很难把那家健身房的费用「花得值」。

collocations: make sure you get your money's worth
feel like you get your money's worth

words.enDefinition: a pack of items sold together at an attractive price

examples.en: I bought a value pack of pens and divided them with my study group.
examples.zh: 我买了一份「优惠装」的笔，给学习小组的同学分了分。

examples.en: The value pack looked cheaper until I checked the weight on both labels.
examples.zh: 我对比了两个标签上的重量才发现，「优惠装」也没显得那么便宜。

words.enDefinition: the purchase price divided by how often something is used

examples.en: My sister calculated the cost per use before buying a waterproof coat for her commute.
examples.zh: 姐姐买通勤防水外套前，先算了算「每次使用成本」。

examples.en: The secondhand textbook had a low cost per use because I needed it all year.
examples.zh: 那本二手教材我一整年都要用，所以「每次使用成本」很低。

words.enDefinition: a saving that seems sensible but costs more in the end

examples.en: Buying the cheapest shoes was a false economy because I had to replace them within two months.
examples.zh: 买最便宜的鞋是「省小钱花大钱」，不到两个月我就换了一双。

examples.en: Skipping the bike service turned out to be a false economy when the chain broke.
examples.zh: 自行车链条断了，我才发现不做保养是「省小钱花大钱」。

collocations: turn out to be a false economy

words.enDefinition: I cannot afford that within my planned spending

examples.en: I'd love to come, but that's outside my budget until I get paid next week.
examples.zh: 我也很想去，但下周发薪之前，「那超出我的预算了」。

examples.en: That hotel looks great, but that's outside my budget for this weekend's trip.
examples.zh: 那家酒店看起来不错，但「它超出了我这周末出游的预算」。

collocations: that's outside my budget right now

words.enDefinition: decide to wait before buying something

examples.en: I put off a purchase when I realised I'd need the money for course materials.
examples.zh: 我意识到那笔钱得留着买课程资料，于是「把另一样东西晚点再买」。

examples.en: It's easy to put off a purchase when you can borrow the same thing.
examples.zh: 同样的东西能借到的话，就很容易「先不买」。

collocations: put off a purchase until payday
decide to put off a purchase

words.enDefinition: pay less for getting an order sent to you

examples.en: We ordered the books together to save on delivery and shared the cost afterwards.
examples.zh: 我们一起订书来「省运费」，之后再分摊花销。

examples.en: I collected the shelf after class to save on delivery and avoid waiting at home.
examples.zh: 下课后我去自取架子，好「省运费」，也不用在家等。

words.enDefinition: the order value needed to qualify for no delivery charge

examples.en: I checked the free shipping threshold before adding a pack of paper to my order.
examples.zh: 我先查了「包邮门槛」，才在订单里加了一包纸。

examples.en: Our order reached the free shipping threshold once we both added the books we needed.
examples.zh: 我们各自把要用的书都加进订单后，金额就达到「包邮门槛」了。

words.enDefinition: the smallest amount you must spend to qualify for something

examples.en: The voucher had a minimum spend of thirty dollars, so I left it unused.
examples.zh: 那张券要求「最低消费金额」三十美元，所以我没用。

examples.en: I asked whether the minimum spend applied when our table used separate checks.
examples.zh: 我问我们这桌分开结账时，是否也有「最低消费金额」的要求。

words.enDefinition: a special starting price offered to new customers

examples.en: The introductory price looked affordable until I saw what the plan would cost after September.
examples.zh: 「首期优惠价」看着挺便宜，直到我看到九月后套餐要多少钱。

examples.en: I wrote down the date when the introductory price for the study app would end.
examples.zh: 我记下了学习应用的「首期优惠价」什么时候结束。

words.enDefinition: a price expressed as a monthly amount for comparison

examples.en: The equivalent monthly cost was lower, but I would have to pay upfront for the year.
examples.zh: 「折合每月费用」更低，但我得先一次付清全年的钱。

examples.en: I calculated the equivalent monthly cost before choosing between two annual gym plans.
examples.zh: 选健身房的两个年度方案之前，我先算了「折合每月费用」。

words.enDefinition: the full amount shown when you are ready to pay

examples.en: The total at checkout was higher than I'd expected once delivery was added.
examples.zh: 加上运费后，「结账时的总额」比我想的要高。

examples.en: I compared the total at checkout on both sites before ordering the same headphones.
examples.zh: 下单买同款耳机前，我比较了两个网站「结账时的总额」。

words.enDefinition: marked down so remaining stock will sell quickly

examples.en: The bread was reduced to clear just before the shop closed for the night.
examples.zh: 快打烊的时候，店里的面包「降价清仓」了。

examples.en: I found a winter coat reduced to clear at a shop near the station.
examples.zh: 我在车站附近一家店里找到一件「降价清仓」的冬外套。

words.enDefinition: a package containing several units of a product

examples.en: I bought a multipack of crisps for our study group's end-of-term picnic.
examples.zh: 我给学习小组的期末野餐买了包「多件组合装」的薯片。

examples.en: The multipack contained six small boxes, so we each took one for the trip.
examples.zh: 「多件组合装」里有六个小盒，我们每人拿了一盒带着出门。

words.enDefinition: pay the regular price without a discount

examples.en: I had to pay full price because I left my student card at home.
examples.zh: 我把学生证落在家里了，只好「付原价」。

examples.en: We didn't want to pay full price with student discounts starting the next morning.
examples.zh: 学生优惠第二天一早就开始，我们「不想付原价」。

collocations: pay full price for a ticket

words.enDefinition: being sold for less than the usual price

examples.en: The cereal I like is on sale this week at the shop by the station.
examples.zh: 车站旁那家店本周在「打折出售」我喜欢的谷物早餐。

examples.en: I waited until the kettle was on sale before getting one for the flat.
examples.zh: 我一直等到电水壶「打折出售」，才给公寓买了一个。

words.enDefinition: reduce what you spend on things you do not need

examples.en: I tried to cut unnecessary spending by bringing coffee instead of buying it on campus.
examples.zh: 我试着自己带咖啡去学校，免得在学校买，以「削减不必要的开支」。

examples.en: We had to cut unnecessary spending to afford the train tickets for our field trip.
examples.zh: 我们得「削减不必要的开支」，才能买得起实地考察要用的火车票。

collocations: look for ways to cut unnecessary spending

words.enDefinition: small extra costs connected with a main activity

examples.en: I kept ten dollars for incidental expenses like luggage storage at the train station.
examples.zh: 我留了十美元，用来付车站行李寄存之类的「附带杂费」。

examples.en: The field trip handout lists incidental expenses separately from transport and accommodation.
examples.zh: 实地考察手册把「附带杂费」和交通、住宿分开列了。

words.enDefinition: switch to a cheaper service with fewer features

examples.en: The website showed how to downgrade a plan without losing access before the renewal date.
examples.zh: 网站上说明了怎样「换成低档套餐」，同时保留续订日期前的使用权限。

examples.en: I wanted to downgrade a plan I'd bought for a course that had already ended.
examples.zh: 我之前为了上课买了一个套餐，现在课结束了，想「换成低档套餐」。

words.enDefinition: a special price for products or services bought together

examples.en: We found a bundle deal that included a train ticket and entry to the exhibition.
examples.zh: 我们找到了一个「捆绑优惠」，里面包括火车票和展览门票。

examples.en: The bundle deal only saved money if I actually used both of the apps.
examples.zh: 只有两个应用我都用得上，这个「捆绑优惠」才省钱。

collocations: sign up for a bundle deal

words.enDefinition: pay for a service as you use it instead of committing in advance

examples.en: I prefer to pay as you go at the gym because I rarely go during exams.
examples.zh: 我更愿意去健身房「按使用付费」，因为备考时基本不去。

examples.en: You can pay as you go for bike rentals if you don't want a membership.
examples.zh: 租自行车不想办会员的话，可以「按使用付费」。

collocations: choose to pay as you go
pay as you go for gym visits

words.enDefinition: an arrangement that charges you each month for ongoing access

examples.en: I started a monthly subscription to the software while I was finishing my final project.
examples.zh: 做毕业项目的收尾工作时，我开通了这款软件的「月度订阅」。

examples.en: The monthly subscription ended just after I handed in the last assignment for that module.
examples.zh: 我交完那门课的最后一次作业没多久，「月度订阅」就到期了。

collocations: sign up for a monthly subscription

words.enDefinition: one level of a subscription with its own price and benefits

examples.en: I chose a cheaper subscription tier because I only needed the basic editing tools.
examples.zh: 我只需要基础编辑工具，就选了一个更便宜的「订阅档位」。

examples.en: The subscription tier we picked lets both of us use the account at once.
examples.zh: 我们选的「订阅档位」允许我们两个人同时用这个账号。

words.enDefinition: a subscription you keep paying for but do not use

examples.en: I found an unused subscription when I went through my expenses after the summer break.
examples.zh: 暑假结束后，我翻开支记录，发现有一项「闲置订阅」。

examples.en: I'd been paying for an unused subscription to an app from my first term.
examples.zh: 第一学期装的那个应用我一直没用，却一直在为这项「闲置订阅」付费。

words.enDefinition: a review of subscriptions and what they are costing you

examples.en: A quick subscription audit showed I was paying for two apps that did the same thing.
examples.zh: 做了个简单的「订阅盘点」后，我发现自己给两个功能一样的应用都付了钱。

examples.en: We added a subscription audit to our routine at the end of each term.
examples.zh: 我们把「订阅盘点」加进了每学期末的例行事项。

words.enDefinition: a limited period of using a service without paying

examples.en: I used the free trial to see whether the app could read my lecture slides.
examples.zh: 我用「免费试用」体验了一下，看这个应用能不能读取我的课件。

examples.en: The free trial ends on Friday, so I've put a reminder in my calendar.
examples.zh: 「免费试用」周五结束，我就在日历里设了个提醒。

collocations: sign up for a free trial

words.enDefinition: end the arrangement that gives you ongoing paid access

examples.en: I couldn't find where to cancel a subscription I had started during orientation week.
examples.zh: 迎新周开通的那项服务，我找不到哪里可以「取消订阅」。

examples.en: The help page explains how to cancel a subscription if you signed up through the app.
examples.zh: 帮助页面说明了如果是从应用里开通的，要如何「取消订阅」。

words.enDefinition: temporarily stop a subscription without ending it permanently

examples.en: I can pause a subscription to the meal service while I'm away for spring break.
examples.zh: 春假外出期间，我可以「暂停订阅」这项配餐服务。

examples.en: The gym lets you pause a subscription during the summer if you're leaving town.
examples.zh: 暑假要离开这座城市的话，健身房允许「暂停订阅」。

collocations: pause a subscription for a month
an option to pause a subscription

words.enDefinition: the date on which a subscription starts another term

examples.en: I checked the subscription renewal date before leaving the country for my summer placement.
examples.zh: 出国做暑期实习前，我查了「订阅续期日」。

examples.en: I didn't notice the subscription renewal date until I opened the settings page.
examples.zh: 我打开设置页面才注意到「订阅续期日」。

words.enDefinition: the next date a charge is due to be billed

examples.en: I checked the next billing date because the cheaper rate was supposed to start in June.
examples.zh: 我查了「下次计费日期」，因为较便宜的价格按说六月才开始。

examples.en: The next billing date falls two days before I get paid for my campus job.
examples.zh: 「下次计费日期」在我的校内兼职发工资前两天。

words.enDefinition: charging for a service once a year

examples.en: I switched to annual billing because I knew I'd use the software throughout the course.
examples.zh: 我换成了「按年计费」，因为我知道整个课程都会用到这个软件。

examples.en: The advertised price assumes annual billing, so the amount due today is much higher.
examples.zh: 广告价是根据「按年计费」的方案折算的，所以今天实际要付的金额高多了。

words.enDefinition: make a payment for something each month

examples.en: I chose to pay monthly for the sports pass because I'm leaving before summer.
examples.zh: 我夏天前就要走，所以体育通行证我选了「按月付款」。

examples.en: Does it cost extra to pay monthly for the same software after the student trial ends?
examples.zh: 学生试用结束后，同一个软件「按月付款」会更贵吗？

words.enDefinition: a charge adjusted to cover only part of a billing period

examples.en: I saw a prorated charge after I switched plans halfway through the month.
examples.zh: 月中换套餐后，我看到一笔「按比例计收的费用」。

examples.en: The first receipt showed a prorated charge because my membership started partway through July.
examples.zh: 因为我的会员是七月过了一段时间才开始的，第一张收据上列的是「按比例计收的费用」。

words.enDefinition: money members regularly pay to belong to a group

examples.en: Our climbing club collects membership dues before the first outdoor trip of the year.
examples.zh: 我们攀岩社在本年度第一次户外出行前收「会员会费」。

examples.en: I checked whether membership dues included the cost of hiring equipment at practice.
examples.zh: 我查了「会员会费」包不包括训练时租用装备的钱。

words.enDefinition: membership that lasts for one year

examples.en: An annual membership would cover both semesters and the summer research period on campus.
examples.zh: 「一年期会员资格」能覆盖两个学期，以及留校做研究的那段暑假。

examples.en: I got an annual membership at the museum because the course visits every month.
examples.zh: 我办了博物馆的「一年期会员资格」，因为课程每个月都安排去参观。

words.enDefinition: the amount you pay for a bus ride

examples.en: The bus fare to campus went up just before I started my weekend job.
examples.zh: 我刚要开始做周末兼职，去学校的「公交车费」就涨了。

examples.en: I kept enough cash for the bus fare in case my phone ran out of battery.
examples.zh: 我留了够付「公交车费」的现金，以防手机没电。

words.enDefinition: money spent on washing and drying clothes

examples.en: I hadn't included laundry costs before I found out how much each dryer cycle was.
examples.zh: 知道烘干机用一次多少钱之前，我都没把「洗衣开销」算进去。

examples.en: We cut our laundry costs by hanging things outside when it was warm enough.
examples.zh: 天气暖和的时候我们把衣服晾在外面，省下了些「洗衣开销」。

words.enDefinition: products for washing, grooming, or looking after your body

examples.en: I made a list of toiletries before going to the supermarket with my flatmate.
examples.zh: 和室友去超市前，我列了张「个人洗护用品」清单。

examples.en: We bought toiletries in our first week and put the home supplies under a separate heading.
examples.zh: 我们第一周就买了「个人洗护用品」，把家居用品另列了一类。

words.enDefinition: items such as notebooks and pens used for studying

examples.en: I bought my school supplies at the campus shop after checking what the course required.
examples.zh: 查清课程要求后，我在校内商店买了「学习用品」。

examples.en: We split the cost of some school supplies because we both needed the same markers.
examples.zh: 我们都需要同款记号笔，就分摊了部分「学习用品」的费用。

words.enDefinition: the amount planned for meals bought away from home

examples.en: My eating-out budget was nearly gone after three group dinners in the same week.
examples.zh: 同一个星期参加三次聚餐后，我的「外出就餐预算」快花光了。

examples.en: I scaled back my eating-out budget once I found a kitchen I could use on campus.
examples.zh: 找到学校里能用的厨房后，我减少了「外出就餐预算」。

words.enDefinition: money spent on transport and other costs during a trip

examples.en: The conference covered some travel expenses, but I still had to pay for local buses.
examples.zh: 会议报销了一部分「出行费用」，但当地的公交车费还是要自己付。

examples.en: My travel expenses were higher this term because the placement was in another city.
examples.zh: 实习在另一座城市，我这学期的「出行费用」比以前高。

words.enDefinition: a choice to give up one financial benefit for another

examples.en: There was a financial trade-off between paying higher rent and spending less on transport.
examples.zh: 付更高的房租还是少花交通费，要做个「金钱上的取舍」。

examples.en: I explained the financial trade-off to my brother before choosing a cheaper phone plan.
examples.zh: 我先跟弟弟讲了「金钱上的取舍」，才选了便宜点的手机套餐。

collocations: a financial trade-off between two options

words.enDefinition: asks what amount someone can comfortably contribute

examples.en: Before we book the hostel, how much can you spare for the whole weekend?
examples.zh: 订青旅前，先说说整个周末「你能腾出多少钱」？

examples.en: How much can you spare this week if we need to replace the frying pan?
examples.zh: 这周要是得换个平底锅，「你能腾出多少钱」？

collocations: how much can you spare this week?
how much can you spare right now?
how much can you spare for the trip?

words.enDefinition: a plan that limits everyday purchases to physical cash

examples.en: I used a cash-only budget on holiday because it made my spending easier to see.
examples.zh: 我度假时用的是「只用现金的预算」，这样花了多少一目了然。

examples.en: A cash-only budget was awkward when the campus bookshop stopped accepting notes and coins.
examples.zh: 校内书店不再收纸币和硬币后，用「只用现金的预算」就不方便了。

words.enDefinition: the distinction between what you need and what you want

examples.en: We discussed needs versus wants before deciding which items to put in the shared budget.
examples.zh: 决定哪些东西列进共同预算之前，我们聊了聊「必需与想要的区别」。

examples.en: The workshop used real receipts to show how students think about needs versus wants.
examples.zh: 讲座用了真实小票，展示学生怎样区分「必需品与想买的东西」。

collocations: sort purchases into needs versus wants
a discussion of needs versus wants

words.enDefinition: switch to a less expensive product or service

examples.en: I decided to trade down to a cheaper phone after seeing what repairs would cost.
examples.zh: 看到维修要多少钱后，我决定「改买低价款」手机。

examples.en: We had to trade down when the tickets we wanted went over our spending limit.
examples.zh: 看中的票超出了支出上限，我们只好「改买低价款」。

collocations: trade down to a cheaper model

words.enDefinition: a list of things you plan to buy

examples.en: I added everything for Friday's dinner to the shopping list before leaving for class.
examples.zh: 出门上课前，我把周五晚餐要买的东西都添进了「购物清单」。

examples.en: I stuck to the shopping list even though the supermarket had a whole aisle of snacks.
examples.zh: 超市虽然有整整一排零食，我还是照着「购物清单」买。

words.enDefinition: charges added on top of a quoted price

examples.en: The added fees made the cheaper ticket more expensive than the one I saw first.
examples.zh: 算上「额外费用」，本来便宜的那张票比我最先看到的还贵。

examples.en: I checked for added fees before paying for a ticket to the student film festival.
examples.zh: 付学生电影节的票钱之前，我查了查有没有「额外费用」。

words.enDefinition: a purchase that costs much more than normal purchases

examples.en: The laptop was a big-ticket purchase, so I compared repair options before replacing it.
examples.zh: 换电脑算一笔「大额消费」，所以换之前我先比较了几种维修方案。

examples.en: I plan each big-ticket purchase around the weeks when I have extra shifts at work.
examples.zh: 每笔「大额消费」，我都会安排在打工班次比较多的那几周。
